Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the mandated wake-visual inspection skill. I’ll then trace the assigned parent, sampled results, inherited optimizer logs, and current rollout evidence before making the single candidate and updating both required documentation files.

The skill requires the prewarm and rollout keyframes to anchor any controller edit, so I’m explicitly pausing policy changes until those images and their matching metrics/diagnostics have been compared. The current contract confirms the candidate must remain non-empty throughout and that formal CFD is out of scope here.

The visual comparison is now complete. The best rollout is actively self-propelled into the central wake and captures nearly horizontally; the inherited sign-asymmetric steering candidate keeps turning/reversing on the right, never acquires that corridor, and times out despite lower RMS force. I’m now checking which body-frame observations are actually exposed so the next hypothesis stays within the public contract and does not smuggle in route or clock information.

The inherited results close two tempting branches: adding `0.05` of extra heading-rate damping delayed capture from `244.547` to `259.160` and cut controller-relative upstream transport by more than half, while sign-gating the rate lead caused a horizon miss. I’m recording that negative evidence first. The remaining bounded test is the opposite, half-size heading-component perturbation: retain the proven target-line lead, slightly reduce only yaw damping, and leave propulsion and all guards untouched.

The visual-first skill has now directly shaped the candidate: propulsion is restored to the replicated `20.25°` anchor, while the only new behavior is a bounded half-size, opposite-sign heading component. The notes and durable guidance both capture why extra damping and sign-based switching failed. I’m moving to the mandated semantic, schema/contract, and editable-boundary checks; no CFD will be run.

The semantic checker exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so it cannot identify a unique baseline. This is the same bookkeeping issue documented in inherited workers. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, then rerunning the check; it does not alter the task or candidate evidence.

The semantic check passes. The Julia runtime is unavailable in this environment, so the executable contract check cannot start; I’ll compensate with the deterministic schema/static guard and retain that limitation in the handoff. I’m rerunning the boundary check after correcting a workspace-path typo in my first invocation.

Completed exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) restores the proven `20.25°` gait and tests bounded `0.025` heading-rate relief.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) contains the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:73) adds the evidence-backed negative lesson on extra heading damping and sign-based rate switching.

Semantic guidance, parameter-schema, candidate-surface, and boundary checks pass. Julia is unavailable, so the executable finite-action check could not run. No CFD was run.
